transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-01-07 16:00 UTC
- Duration: 52 minutes
- Attendees: Sofia Morales (Redwood AE), Derek Chan (Redwood SE), Priya Kumar (Redwood CSM), Liam O'Neil (TidePort VP Eng), Mei Zhang (TidePort Head of ML), Carlos Reyes (TidePort Security), Anita Patel (TidePort Procurement)

Quick summary (auto):
- TidePort is evaluating a contract uplift for increased capacity and adding EU region with data residency constraints.
- Security team needs SOC2 + ISO artifacts, KMS options, and one-week benchmark run for their routing flows.
- Next: pricing scenarios from AE, SE to run benchmark, CSM to schedule pilot kickoff.

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I think we can kick off—happy new year, by the way. Quick run through agenda: pricing scenarios, EU region onboarding and data residency, security asks, and pilot kickoff timeline.
[00:12] Liam: Thanks Sofia, and same to you. We're sort of on an accelerated path, we need a bump for Q1 traffic, and the legal team is pressing on data residency in EU—so we wanted to align.
[00:22] Mei: Yeah, our inference volume spiked over the holidays, we need to make sure we don't hit throttles. Also we ran a couple of latency tests and saw tail latency jump on long sequences.
[00:33] Derek: Got it. When you say tail latency, is that on our hosted API or on the dedicated pool?
[00:38] Mei: Hosted. We tried both actually, but 95th went up when sequence len > 1k. Might be batching interaction with prefix cache.
[00:47] Derek: Okay, that's consistent with continuous batch behavior; we saw similar in the logs. If you can share a sample distribution, we can recommend quantization/batching and maybe a small dedicated pool for the heavy endpoints.
[00:58] Liam: Budget's the thing. Procurement wants a short-term uplift option — like 6 months — before committing to an annual reserved plan.
[01:06] Anita: Correct, we want the flexibility to validate the EU region before a longer contract. Also need to ensure contract language covers PII handling in EU.
[01:15] Priya: Noted. Our standard is to provide a 6-month uplift addendum — we've done that for other customers. Sofia, you'll send scenarios, right?
[01:22] Sofia: Yep, I'll put together 6-month and annual scenarios with region add-ons. I'll also include estimated unit economics after routing policy changes.
[01:30] Carlos: From security side, we need SOC2 Type II, ISO27001, and KMS integration choices. Also audit logs retention options.
[01:39] Derek: We can do KMS via bring-your-own-key to the private control plane, or integrate with cloud KMS for Dedicated. For hosted we have customer-managed keys via HSM—though I should say the transcript might call it "H S M"—but basically it's supported.
[01:52] Carlos: If hosted supports BYOK, how is key sovereignty handled?
[01:56] Derek: Keys are stored in the KMS you control; Redwood only sees wrapped keys. For the EU region, if you pick a private deployment path we can ensure keys never leave the VPC. There's a tradeoff: fully private on-prem gives most control but longer lead time.
[02:12] Mei: Lead time is a concern — we can't wait 8 weeks for on-prem. Can Redwood provision an EU dedicated pool in 2-3 weeks?
[02:20] Derek: For Dedicated in EU, 2-3 weeks is realistic if there's capacity and we have the contract agreed, but provisioning windows can vary. There's also the option to route EU traffic to a hosted EU region with data residency controls and an SLA for deletion/retention.
[02:34] Liam: Is the hosted EU region sufficient for our regulators? Some partners require that data never leaves the EU.
[02:40] Carlos: Exactly. We need confirmation that logs and request bodies are stored only in-region.
[02:46] Priya: We have an EU-hosted configuration where request payloads are kept in-region and audit logs can be retained per customer policy. I can share the doc with the retention settings.
[02:55] Sofia: I'll attach the EU region compliance note with the pricing doc.
[03:00] Anita: Also, procurement wants sample contract wording for data residency.
[03:04] Sofia: We'll provide a redline-ready clause.
[03:07] Mei: On benchmarks — we're planning a two-tier test: one is functional correctness across prompts, second is a load run with our real traffic shape. We need a baseline script.
[03:16] Derek: We'll share a benchmark script that runs your production distribution and measures p95/p99 and cost per million tokens. We'll also give guidance on batching windows and quantization.
[03:25] Mei: Great. Can we run it in the EU region?
[03:28] Derek: Yes, if you provision a temporary EU instance we can run the benchmark against a hosted EU model or a dedicated test node. The benchmark will need ~24-48 hours to be statistically meaningful for tail latency.
[03:39] Liam: That timeline works. Anita, any procurement blockers?
[03:42] Anita: We need pricing flexibility, and a statement of support SLAs for the uplift period. Also change control for adding regions mid-term.
[03:50] Sofia: For uplifts we can offer a mid-term amendment with a fixed uplift rate and an option to convert to annual with credit for the uplift spend. Slas for uplift mirror the dedicated SLA if you opt into dedicated capacity.
[04:02] Carlos: Can you confirm escalation path? Who do we call for incidents during pilot?
[04:07] Priya: CSM will be primary, with SE escalation to on-call infra. We'll share an on-call contact list in the kickoff doc.
[04:14] Derek: And for incident post-mortem, we provide token-level traces and tail latency breakdowns—though sometimes the automated transcription calls it "token level brake down"—but yes we'll give the traces.
[04:26] Mei: About model variants — we use a mix of open models and fine-tuned homegrown models. If we move heavy endpoints to dedicated, what's the deployment model?
[04:36] Derek: You can pin model versions, perform canary rollouts, and we support model variants. For fine-tuned artifacts you can bring them or we can host them in a private bucket. Note on quantization: some of the very small FP formats change output slightly — we'll validate with your eval set.
[04:52] Liam: Are there unit-cost savings if we do a dedicated pool for only the heavy endpoints? We want a hybrid approach.
[04:58] Sofia: Yes, we often see 15-40% cost improvements by routing high-volume endpoints to dedicated with caching and prefix-KV enabled. We'll run numbers in the scenario docs.
[05:10] Mei: One more question on caching — we rely on long context reuse. Does Redwood support long-lived KV caches across sessions?
[05:17] Derek: Yes, we support persistent KV cache for session affinity; it's configurable. The only caveat is cache eviction policy needs to be tuned for your access patterns.
[05:25] Carlos: Regarding logging: does Redwood keep full request payloads in logs? We need redaction options.
[05:30] Priya: We have redaction rules and can set tokenization-level redaction. We'll include the redaction options doc.
[05:36] Anita: For procurement, will an uplift be invoiced monthly or up front?
[05:40] Sofia: For 6-month uplift we can do monthly billing or pre-pay with a small discount. We'll provide both options.
[05:46] Liam: Sounds fine. On the legal side, we want an indemnity clause regarding data residency breaches. Is that standard?
[05:53] Sofia: We can include standard indemnities; final legal review required. We'll flag that for legal teams.
[05:58] Carlos: One technical ask: can you provide an architecture diagram showing EU routing, KMS, and log flow — we need it for our auditors.
[06:06] Derek: Absolutely. I'll include an architecture diagram with the flow: client -> EU ingress -> model routing (hosted/dedicated) -> KMS wrap/unwrap in-region -> audit logs in-region.
[06:18] Mei: Great. For the benchmark data — we'll need both latency and quality metrics. Can Redwood help run a quality regression check against our eval set?
[06:26] Derek: We can run your eval prompts through the model variants and return BLEU-ish metrics and qualitative mismatch examples. Note that open model names sometimes get transcribed oddly, but we'll deliver real outputs and an analysis sheet.
[06:37] Anita: Will the pilot require any additional network peering or IP allowances?
[06:40] Derek: For dedicated in VPC, you'll need to allow outbound to the provisioned nodes; we'll share the IP ranges. For hosted EU, generally no peering but there are IP allowlist options for stricter setups.
[06:51] Liam: OK. Let's talk timeline: we want pilot in mid-Jan. Is that still feasible?
[06:56] Priya: If we get the uplift PO this week and Derek's team has the benchmark infra, mid-Jan pilot kickoff is doable. I'll tentatively book week of Jan 19 for kickoff per earlier note.
[07:07] Sofia: I'll aim to send pricing and the region compliance doc by Jan 12. Derek will share the benchmark script by Jan 11.
[07:14] Mei: One last technical nuance — we've seen prompt truncation on longer prompts with the hosted default tokenizer. Could that be tokenizer mismatch?
[07:22] Derek: Possible. We'll check tokenization and sequence length handling and, if needed, recommend a tokenizer alignment or a model variant with a larger context window.
[07:29] Liam: Anything else?
[07:31] Carlos: A short item — can you confirm data deletion timeline if we terminate?
[07:36] Priya: Standard is 30 days for hosted, immediate wipe for private on-prem clauses can be included. We'll add that to the compliance doc.
[07:44] Sofia: Great. Let's go to a quick recap and owners.
[07:47] Sofia: Recap: Sofia sends pricing scenarios + redline clause (owner: Sofia) by Jan 12. Derek shares benchmark script + architecture diagram by Jan 11. Priya schedules kickoff and shares retention/redaction docs by Jan 14. Carlos/TidePort to send regulatory list by Jan 13.
[08:05] Liam: That works. Procurement — Anita, anything else?
[08:07] Anita: No, just need the PO template and invoice terms.
[08:10] Sofia: We'll include PO template.
[08:12] Mei: Appreciate it.
[08:13] Derek: Quick note — one optimization we might propose is a read-through cache on model outputs for some inference classes. Saves cost. We'll outline where it fits.
[08:21] Liam: Cool. If no other items, thank you everyone.
[08:24] Sofia: Thanks all, we'll follow up with docs.
[08:26] (call ends)
